So what is the significance of this discovery?

When you have a complete DNA sequence, you can use it as a template for making sense of cheap DNA data.

Cheap DNA sequencing chops the DNA into small pieces (shotgun sequencing) and then determines the sequence of each little piece. It's cheap but hard to assemble all the little bits into a big picture.

Having a high-quality reference sequence makes it much easier to figure out how all the cheap little DNA fragments relate to each other. It's kind of like the picture on a puzzle box.
